I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, since I was a young man following my father through the fields. At 63, my back isn't what it used to be, and my son moved to Shijiazhuang years ago, so it's mostly me and my wife now. We manage about 8 mu. I'm not going to complicate things.

Here, everyone does wheat and maize rotation. Winter wheat goes in around Hanlu in October, and after we harvest it in June, we turn around and plant summer maize in the same fields. That's what my father did, that's what I do. The government purchase price is predictable, the agrochemical shop knows what I need, and I've done it so many times I can judge the soil by feel.

For wheat I'll use the improved variety — Jimai series, the kind I've bought from the same shop in town for years. Hybrid wheat seed is too expensive and I'm not convinced. I'll base fertilize at planting with compound fertilizer, then topdress urea at jointing in spring. I water before winter to get good root establishment, again in early spring, and at heading if it's been dry. That's three times, sometimes four if the weather is strange. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids and rust near heading. Rotary till before sowing, as always.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the shop has that the neighbors are using this year. The yields are real. I direct seed right after wheat harvest, no tilling, to catch the moisture. Summer rains usually carry us but I'll run the tube well once in a dry stretch. I topdress with urea around the 10-leaf stage. Spray once or twice for fall armyworm and leaf blight.

I'm not going to try cotton or peanuts this year. At my age, wheat and maize are predictable, I know the work, and I can do most of it with the small tractor.
